source.authors: Sauer DJ, Yopak KE, Radford CA
source.title: Ontogenetic development of inner ear hair cell organization in the New Zealand carpet shark Cephaloscyllium isabellum

where: Results, ontogeny of hair cell number (sentence returned by WebFetch in two adjoining pieces, reassembled); page prints 'This is an open-access article distributed under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution License (CC BY).'
quote: For example, the smallest C. isabellum had an approximated 4,830 saccular HCs, while the largest had a 3 fold increase to approximately 14,492.
conditions: Smallest individual (about 40 cm total length). 18 individuals (12 females, 6 males) from commercial fishers at Leigh, New Zealand, total length 40.5 to 82.0 cm; saccular count rose about threefold from the smallest to the largest fish (4,830 to 14,492), and the same Results text gives saccular macular area of 792,153 µm2 in a 40 cm juvenile and 1,524,930 µm2 in an 81 cm adult, so macula area rose about 1.9-fold, less than the count; utricle, lagena and macula neglecta are not covered by this value. Anatomy only; hearing not tested.
note: Name: the paper spells isabellum; FishBase (search-result title) and desk-d277's note say the accepted spelling is isabella (Eschmeyer's Catalog entry not opened by this unit; unchecked). Not on main (grep of docs/ for isabellum and 1034891 found only desk progress notes d204/d277/d186 recording earlier declines for lack of a trait key; sensory_anatomy now exists). Licence: CC BY sentence printed on the copy read; Crossref not queried. Same quote supports the smallest and largest records.

method: stereomicroscope images of the stapes from dry skulls, measured in ImageJ
conditions: Ten dry skulls from the Belgrade veterinary comparative collection (road kills and clinical cases), tympanic cavity opened on both sides; per-measurement n varies from 3 to 9; sex and age not stated here. Row cells in order: stapedial footplate length (mm), footplate width (mm), footplate area (mm2), footplate index. The row lists area 1.69 mm2, which is larger than length times width (1.542 x 0.4967 = 0.77 mm2) and than an ellipse of those axes (0.60 mm2), so the area is not filed; the index 299.35 differs from length/width x 100 (about 310), consistent with means of per-specimen ratios. Other species rows in the same table are literature values. Anatomy only; hearing not tested.
